title: State Management with Riverpod: Patterns That Scaled My Apps
excerpt: How Riverpod's provider architecture helped me untangle complex UI state in Flutter apps, from prototype to production.

content.text: In any non‑trivial Flutter app, state is the hidden dependency that ties views together. When I started building ROT, a screen‑time tracker with multiple dashboards, I quickly realized that a naive approach — storing everything in a single Bloc or a handful of ChangeNotifiers — would become a maintenance nightmare.

Riverpod's provider model let me split the domain into focused units: a ScreenTimeRepository provider, a WeeklyStats state provider, and a GoalAlert provider that listens to changes. Each provider owns its lifecycle, so I could unit‑test the repository without touching the UI, and the UI could simply watch the relevant provider without knowing where the data came from.
A well‑scoped provider is a contract: it tells you what can change, not how it changes.
content.author: Roshan Lal Yogi

content.text: By the time I added the accountability features, the architecture had already proven itself. Adding a new screen required only a few lines of provider definitions, and the existing UI automatically re‑rendered when the underlying state changed. The result was a codebase that stayed readable even as the feature set grew.
